topic: Part 5 Test 1 — Sydney-Perth kill-shot post-c4-patches verification
change_summary: Decider applied 6 patches (H0, H1, H2, H3, H5, H6, H7) from c4 review in commits 571a3d6 (KILLSHOT-SH patches) and 2cb0c98. Verification round: did the patches land cleanly, did they preserve grammar, did they introduce any new defender-exploitable surface?
our_argument_summary: Test 1 (Sydney-Perth) argues V13 Finsler is calibration not prediction, fails on SYD-BUE (V12 -73%, V13 -8.4% via unpublished n(r)), self-disagrees by 460 km Finsler vs MDS, and the disc-radius implies a factor-of-8 rim-circumnavigation discrepancy that refraction cannot dissolve because ships travel through water. Verdict: Misleading.

holes_found.description: GRAMMAR BUG — H5 INSERTION MALFORMED. The H5 patch (calibration-linkage sentence) was inserted into the Summary mid-clause, producing a textual mess. Current Summary text reads verbatim: 'This is not a prediction confirmed — it is iterative curve-fitting with undefined parameters,  The disc radius (20,015 km) that sets the rim circumference is the same parameter the V13 coordinate system uses to map every other city pair, including Sydney–Perth: the two tests are not independent. applied to calibration data.' Three defects: (a) double space after 'parameters,' with the next character a capital 'T' (no period — capitalized continuation after comma is a textual fault), (b) the H5 sentence interrupts a previously-complete clause ('iterative curve-fitting with undefined parameters, applied to calibration data') leaving 'applied to calibration data' stranded as a fragment after the H5 sentence closes with a period, (c) the orphan fragment ' applied to calibration data.' begins with a leading space and reads as a typo. A dome defender reading the Summary will see broken prose at the most-quoted closer of the kill-shot. The H5 content itself (linkage between SYD-PER calibration and rim test sharing the disc-radius parameter) is strong; the integration is what failed.
holes_found.recommendation: Re-patch the Summary closer. Either (a) place H5 BEFORE the 'This is not a prediction confirmed' sentence: 'The disc radius (20,015 km) that sets the rim circumference is the same parameter the V13 coordinate system uses to map every other city pair, including Sydney–Perth: the two tests are not independent. This is not a prediction confirmed — it is iterative curve-fitting with undefined parameters, applied to calibration data.' OR (b) restore the original closer intact and append H5 as a final sentence: 'This is not a prediction confirmed — it is iterative curve-fitting with undefined parameters, applied to calibration data. The disc radius (20,015 km) that sets the rim circumference is the same parameter the V13 coordinate system uses to map every other city pair, including Sydney–Perth: the two tests are not independent.' Option (b) preserves the punchy 'curve-fitting … applied to calibration data' as the lead. Either fixes the orphan fragment.

holes_found.description: H1 PATCH INTRODUCED A NEW UNSOURCED ANCHOR AT A DIFFERENT LATITUDE. The H1 patch replaced the c4 'satellite-tracked circumnavigation records and altimetry of the Antarctic coast measure ~13,700 km' with: 'The globe-predicted 70° S parallel circumference is 2π × 6,371 × cos(70°) = 13,691 km (~13,700 km); recorded southern-ocean circumnavigation routes at 55–60° S log ~20,000 km per lap — either figure is far below the dome's ~111,800 km prediction.' This IMPROVES the 13,700 km figure (it is now a verifiable derivation from globe geometry rather than an unsourced empirical claim — good fix). But the patch added a NEW empirical claim: 'recorded southern-ocean circumnavigation routes at 55–60° S log ~20,000 km per lap.' Three defects: (a) no citation provided, (b) the 55–60°S latitude is NOT the same as the 70°S latitude that the Antarctic-coast computation uses (rim test stays at 17,791 km radius mapped to 70°S, so 55–60°S routes are at a different distance from the rim), (c) a defender can plausibly object: 'You showed the globe prediction at 70°S (13,691 km) and then quoted ship-log ~20,000 km per lap at 55–60°S — those are different latitudes; the globe prediction at 55–60°S would be 2π × 6,371 × cos(57.5°) ≈ 21,500 km, which is suspiciously close to your ~20,000 km figure and could just as well support a globe vs. dome.' The 'either figure is far below the dome's ~111,800 km prediction' framing partially neutralizes this (both are still orders below the dome) but the latitude mismatch is a real seam. ISS-2481 was closed but the close was premature.
holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) drop the 55–60°S sentence and rely on the globe-geometry derivation alone: 'The globe-predicted 70°S parallel circumference is 2π × 6,371 × cos(70°) = 13,691 km — far below the dome's ~111,800 km prediction at the same parallel.' Cleanest. OR (b) keep the 55–60°S anchor but add the corresponding globe-circumference prediction at that latitude (2π × 6,371 × cos(57.5°) ≈ 21,500 km) so the comparison is apples-to-apples within latitude. OR (c) cite a specific source (CIA Factbook Antarctic coastline, IBCSO bathymetry) for the 55–60°S figure. Option (a) is the lowest-effort and bulletproof.

holes_found.description: H4 (SPHERE-IN-DISGUISE CLOSER) — still open as expected. Current closer reads: 'A defender invoking a Finsler metric that compresses 125,760 km of dome-Euclidean distance into 13,700 km of fuel-burn distance is admitting the disc is a sphere in disguise — at that point the dome has lost its geometric distinctiveness and become a renamed globe projection.' This is the c4 closer unchanged, still vulnerable to the 'we predict differently on other tests' rebuttal. The decider correctly routed ISS-2484 to analyst as EXP-563 (class_hint: deep-attack); no need to escalate again — flagging as carry-over so M3 enforcement keeps it visible until EXP-563 lands.
holes_found.recommendation: No action this cycle — EXP-563 (assigned to analyst) is the right path. When EXP-563 returns, integrate per normal expansion procedure and re-verify on a subsequent curmudgeon pass.

stronger_arguments.description: Once the H5 grammar bug is fixed, the Summary becomes the strongest closer in any kill-shot — naming the disc radius as the shared parameter directly inverts the dome's only escape (treat SYD-PER and rim as separable tests). Worth promoting the H5 sentence to lead-with rather than tail-of-Summary once re-patched.

The 'ships move through water; refraction bends light' framing is the strongest physical anchor in Problem 4. Currently it appears once. Consider repeating it in the §7.1 derivation cross-ref to compound the rhetorical force — but doing so risks the cross-reference duplication issue H8 from c4 flagged.

kernel_of_truth.description: The c4 patches landed substantive structural improvements: H0 closes the 'use a different projection' escape (data/sections.json#part5 paragraph 'Nor does projection choice rescue this'), H2 brings in the dome author's own V22 evolution-log concession (paragraph containing 'Version 22 of the model explicitly stated'), H3 distinguishes the rim failure from the V12 cross-equator failure, H6 strengthens the TLDR (now leads with the factor-of-eight rim discrepancy), H7 removes the '~800%' rounding nit. Five of six patches are clean wins; only H5's integration mechanics produced the grammar bug. The kill-shot is genuinely stronger after c4 patching than before — the bug is presentation, not substance.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Genuine structural improvements do not exempt the review from the grammar bug — readers of the Summary will see broken prose right at the closer (data/sections.json#part5 contains the verbatim orphan fragment 'applied to calibration data.' after the H5 sentence). The H5 substance (calibration and rim share the disc radius parameter) is the strongest argument in Test 1 but it is currently buried mid-orphan-fragment. A 5-minute re-patch (per the recommendation on this review's H5 hole) converts five clean wins into six.

deeper_analysis: Five-of-six clean patches plus one malformed integration. The H5 grammar bug is mechanical: the patch inserted between an incomplete clause and its tail, rather than at a sentence boundary. This is a recurring failure mode for sed-style insertion patches into prose with subordinate clauses — the inserter has to identify the sentence boundary, not just a comma. A pre-write sentence-validation step in the decider's patch tooling would catch this (count sentences before and after; require period before insertion point if next char is capital). The H1 latitude mismatch is more interesting: it shows that what looks like a clean fix (replace one ~13,700 km anchor with another) can introduce a subtler problem (different latitude). A defender skilled in geometric arguments would seize the 55–60°S vs 70°S mismatch immediately. The fix (option (a) — drop the 55–60°S sentence) is low-effort and preserves the strongest version of Problem 4. ISS-2484 H4 sphere-in-disguise rebuttal is the real outstanding deep-attack work and is correctly assigned to analyst EXP-563; nothing for this review to add beyond carry-over flagging.

citations_verified: 2π × 6,371 × cos(70°) = 13,691 km — globe geometry derivation, mathematically correct (verified: cos(70°)=0.342, 2π×6371×0.342=13,690.7 km, rounds to 13,691)
Disc radius 20,015 km → rim circumference 2π × 20,015 = 125,760 km — verified (2π×20015=125,759.9)
70°S parallel under linear AE r = 20,015 × (90-70)/180 = 17,791 km × 2π = 111,800 km — verified
V22 quote 'Southern arc distances 2× too long — FAILS. Globe wins cross-equator.' — quote present in dome author's evolution-log per §7.1 derivation
citations_failed: 'recorded southern-ocean circumnavigation routes at 55–60° S log ~20,000 km per lap' — UNSOURCED. No specific reference. Plausible (Volvo Ocean Race / Vendée Globe lap distances are in this range) but no citation provided. The latitude (55–60°S) does not match the comparison latitude (70°S) used elsewhere in Problem 4.

summary_for_decider: c5 verifies c4 patches landed: H0/H2/H3/H6/H7 clean, H5 substance landed BUT integration is grammatically malformed (orphan fragment 'applied to calibration data' after H5 sentence) — major hole, single sed-fix to resolve. H1 patch introduced a new minor unsourced anchor (55–60°S routes vs 70°S comparison latitude) — moderate hole, prefer dropping the 55–60°S sentence. H4 (ISS-2484, EXP-563) correctly assigned to analyst, carry-over flagged. Queue reason had ISS-2480/2481 H-numbering typo — decider housekeeping only. Recommend: 1 patch for H5 grammar fix, 1 patch for H1 sentence drop, then re-verify on c6.
